rationale: The 24-component layer is stable (mean bootstrap stability 0.812) and is the level at which the atlas is actually reproducible, so it should remain canonical and frozen.
It is NOT the level at which the atlas is interpretable: mean class purity is 0.35 and only 13/24 components reach high interpretive confidence.

Grouping is reproducible (bootstrap 0.969) but geometrically weak (silhouette 0.095), so the group layer should be treated as an interpretive overlay that can be revised, never as the frozen numerical basis.
A hierarchy keeps both properties: numbers from the components, meaning from the themes.

A_24_canonical.description: Use all 24 latent components directly as BSV coordinates.
A_24_canonical.interpretability: low–moderate — 11/24 components are only moderately interpretable and mean class purity is 0.35
A_24_canonical.extensibility: high — new analytes project without changing the basis
A_24_canonical.clinical_usability: poor — 24 weakly-named axes are not communicable
A_24_canonical.verdict: retain as the CANONICAL numerical layer, not as the reported BSV

B_compressed.description: Replace the 24 components with ~14 higher-order coordinates.
B_compressed.interpretability: moderate — groups gain names but lose component detail
B_compressed.stability: grouping bootstrap reproducibility 0.969 but silhouette only 0.095
B_compressed.extensibility: moderate — a new chemistry may not fit existing groups
B_compressed.verdict: not sufficient alone — discards resolution the atlas actually has

C_hierarchical.description: 24 latent components (canonical, frozen) → higher-order biochemical themes (reported) → optional visual summary.
C_hierarchical.interpretability: good — evidence is traceable from a reported theme back to components, bands and reference analytes
C_hierarchical.stability: inherits component stability; group layer is re-derivable and versionable
C_hierarchical.extensibility: high — the numerical layer never changes when the ontology is revised
